learning_outcomes.text: Assess cleanrooms from theoretical and practical aspects and initiate planning processes for the realization of cleanrooms.
Work in cleanroom environments with full knowledge of the required behaviors and the most important laboratory properties.
Evaluate and implement cleanroom operating modes regarding energy minimization.

Theoretically and practically realize thick-film and SMD circuits from layout through various manufacturing steps to 'assembly and connection technology', taking into account the aspect of ecological sustainability.
Analyze the energy consumption of embedded systems at different levels (hardware, software, system).
Design algorithms and software to operate efficiently with limited resources (power, energy, memory).
Perform and evaluate energy measurements on real systems.
Understand Edge Computing concepts in energy-constrained scenarios.

syllabus_topics: Contamination aspects in the manufacturing of microsystems
Definition of clean media and cleanroom classes
Clothing and behavior in the cleanroom
Concepts for energy minimization of cleanrooms
Practical work to deepen one of the topics covered in the lecture
Basic knowledge of monolithic, hybrid and SMD circuit assembly
Selected technologies viewed under their ecological sustainability aspect
Practical implementation of contents in a lab parallel to the lecture
Designing algorithms and software to operate efficiently under limited resources such as computing power, energy, and memory

Different optimization strategies at all levels of software development (selection of suitable data structures and algorithms, memory-saving programming techniques, optimization of execution times and energy profiles)
Systematic trade-off between performance requirements and energy saving
Developing robust and sustainable software solutions in resource-constrained environments

assessment_methods.method: Written assignment and presentation for Energy-Efficient Cleanroom Technology
Exam (60 min) or oral examination (20 min) for Hybrid Integration in connection with Sustainability Aspects
Exam (60 min) or written assignment for System Design of Low Power Architectures

assessment_rules: The module grade for MECB410A is formed by combining the partial examinations MECB412A and MECB413A. MECB411A (Energy-Efficient Cleanroom Technology) is an ungraded event with a written assignment and presentation. MECB412A (Hybrid Integration in connection with Sustainability Aspects) can be a 60-minute written exam or a 20-minute oral exam. MECB413A (System Design of Low Power Architectures) can be a 60-minute written exam or a written assignment.
